missed_quarantine: wrong-result: the 'Total' share of metabolites with a compartment is inverted. TRIGGER: TmodelStats(struct('rxns',{{'R1'}}, 'mets',{{'a[c]';'b[c]';'glc'}}, 'S',sparse([1;-1;0]))). EXPECTED: [2, 2/3]. Evident intent: comment line 112 'Total metabolite with compartment (should be 100%)' and line 120, which computes each compartment's share as nMetsInComp / nMets. The header (line 2) says the function 'Can also be used on a normal model', and a COBRA model may contain metabolite ids without a '[x]' suffix.
why: The test's fixture has a '[x]' suffix on every metabolite, so total = nMets and 4\4 = 4/4 = 1. That hides the inversion at line 123, which is exactly what the 'Total ... should be 100%' row exists to report. Every other expected value is hand-derived and correct. Confidence moderate: inside modelBorgifier, verifyModelBorg forces '[x]' on every metabolite, so the defect appears only on the documented 'normal model' input.
suggestion: Add a plain-model case with one metabolite without a '[x]' suffix and assert Total = [count, count/nMets], then quarantine as wrong-result (line 123), or have the lead record why such a model is out of scope.
